decision_rule: Best-of-8 per arm at tolerance 1e-4. CAUSAL CLAIM: good arm (quarter morph from good scaffold) reaches <= 6.3246+1e-3 AND bad arm (full morph from trap scaffold) reaches >= 6.6569-1e-3 -> the scaffold causes the outcome; the morph inherits its starting basin and the compress phase's job is fully captured by the scaffold it produces. If good arm fails, the compress DYNAMICS (not just its endpoint) matter. If bad arm escapes, the trap is not scaffold-determined. C14 is retained as a documented pilot: its good arm used the wrong tau path (full morph from a quarter scaffold), so its inconclusive result does not bear on this test.
extraction: Same scaffolds as C14 (scripts/extract_scaffold.js on C11). Corrected: good scaffold runs under harden-quarter-morphonly (tau 0.25->0, the path that produced it); bad scaffold under harden-morphonly (tau 1->0). Each morph now exactly reproduces the path that originally followed its scaffold; only the compress phase is skipped.
hypothesis: The scaffold causes the morph's outcome. With the tau path corrected (C14's flaw), transplanting cross n=5's good scaffold under its native quarter morph rescues it to 6.3246, while the trap scaffold under its native full morph stays trapped at 6.6569.
question: Does the scaffold cause the morph's outcome (corrected causal test)?
title: Scaffold transplant v2: matched tau paths
